artists.biography: Carter the Unstoppable Sex Machine (frequently shortened to Carter USM) are an English indie rock band formed in 1988 by singer Jim "Jim Bob" Morrison and guitarist Les "Fruitbat" Carter. They made their name with a distinctive style of power pop, fusing samples, sequenced basses and drum machines with rock 'n' roll guitars and off-beat wordplay-loaded lyrics. They reached the height of their fame in 1992. Over the following years the band took on new members, topping out as a six-piece, but struggled to regain their earlier popularity. They initially split up in 1998 after releasing seven albums.

30 Something, released in February 1991, is the second studio album by Carter the Unstoppable Sex Machine, blending electronic and rock elements characteristic of the band's style. The album was recorded quickly, reportedly in 20 days on an 8-track setup, which contributed to its raw, energetic sound. Musically, it combines punk-inflected rock with electronic beats and samples, reflecting the band's innovative approach to merging genres during the early 1990s.

This album marked a significant step in Carter USM's discography, solidifying their presence in the UK alternative scene. It achieved commercial success, reaching number 8 on the UK Albums Chart and earning a Gold certification, indicating strong sales. The album spawned notable singles such as "Anytime Anyplace Anywhere," which helped expand their fanbase. Critically, 30 Something was well received for its sharp, witty lyrics and distinctive sound, capturing the zeitgeist of British youth culture at the time.

Released on the Chrysalis label, 30 Something remains a key work in Carter the Unstoppable Sex Machine's catalog, showcasing their unique fusion of electronic music and rock with socially conscious themes. Its impact is reflected in its enduring popularity, leading to later reissues and deluxe editions that celebrate its legacy.
